full_judgment: 32. It is in the FIR that when the informant went out in search of deceased he heard from Rashed and Shah Alam (PW 2) that the deceased was seen going towards Muradpur Madrasha Road with Raju, Jamal and 2/3 other boys PW 1 also said so in his evidence. Rashed was withheld without explanation. So presumption would be that had he been examined he would not have supported the prosecution case. PW 2 said that at 6-00 AM he saw the deceased to go towards Madrasha Road with Raju, Jamal and Dulal. At night when PW 1 was searching for Shimul he (PW 2) informed him (PW 1) that he saw the deceased to go towards Muradpur with Raju, Jamal and Dulal. So we find inconsistencies in the evidence of PWs 1 and 2. PW 5 said that Raju, Jamal and their associates called and took away the deceased from their residence. He informed his father of this fact, but the father did not say so. If PW 2 would have said the names of those accused persons with whom he allegedly had seen the deceased to go then their names would have found place in the FIR. PW 11 did not say that in his presence Raju, Jamal and Dulal called and took away the deceased from their residence. Moreover, his presence in the house at the material time was not supported by his father PW 1 and brother PW 5. Absence of the names of those two accused persons as the boys called and took away the deceased in the FIR casts serious doubt in this regard. None besides PW 1 supported PW 2 as to seeing the deceased to go with those three accused persons. Moreover, Dulal was not named in the FIR. On the above reasons, the prosecution could not prove beyond reasonable doubt that the deceased was lastly seen in the company of those three accused persons or they called and took away the deceased from his house in the evening.
